open_risks: The active Protect Main Branch ruleset requires one approval and CI checks; this was satisfied for real on PR #20 (uzom-a's independent code-owner review) and the branch is merged to main.

GET /health, GET /health/ready and POST /v1/requests are implemented and tested but not yet frozen through a joint two-person contract PR review — mark frozen@0.1.0 once both engineers have signed off. Contract version was 0.3.0 vs CHANGELOG.md's 0.1.0 (a real inconsistency, since fixed to 0.1.0 on both sides).

Operational health routes reject requests carrying tunnel/proxy forwarding headers by design (SecurityConfiguration.directProbeOnly()). GET /health/ready correctly returns HTTP 401 through the public tunnel; GET /health and the POST /v1/requests cases pass. Confirmed from both Person One's Mac/iPhone and, on 2026-09-22, Person Two's own Windows PC — the ADR-005 deferral for her own-machine API run is resolved.

AWS staging is deferred (ADR-004) — no budget available right now, even for the near-$0/month minimal design in docs/runbooks/aws-staging-setup.md. The Phase 0 connected checkpoint uses a cloudflared Quick Tunnel instead; revisit AWS no later than Phase 3, when Twilio needs a stable (non-rotating) webhook URL a Quick Tunnel can't provide.

Backend has no Redis dependency or Redis readiness check, even though infra/compose.yml and docker-compose.yml provision Redis. Either wire it in when something actually needs it, or drop it from Compose — don't let 'provisioned but unused' stand as if it were tested.
PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER changed to com.abubakarsidiq01.plug.app101 (com.plug.app was already claimed by another Apple account) and committed to project.pbxproj.

Windows CI passed dependency installation, production web build, browser tests, backend startup, the full local Bruno collection (4 requests, 4 tests, 11 assertions) and state parsing on 16b9c57. Hosted CI does not verify interactive Docker Desktop/WSL setup on Person Two's machine; that work is deferred to her first Phase 1 session under ADR-005.
